$comment: Model prices in USD per million tokens. This is DATA, not constants in
code: a price change is a new row appended here, never an edit to an
existing one, so a run recorded in March stays costed at March's prices.
effective_from is the date the figure was CONFIRMED, not the date it
actually took effect -- we do not know that, and back-dating it would be
a lie in a file that looks authoritative. A run older than the earliest
effective_from is reported as unpriced rather than costed at a rate we
cannot vouch for on that date.
effective_to is null for the currently-effective row. Superseding a row
means setting its effective_to and appending a new one.
Every row holds the same ratios against its base input price: cache read
5x. tests/test_cost.py asserts this across the whole table so that a typo
in a future row fails loudly instead of quietly mispricing runs.
